clue.text: The Texan's topping!

parts.note: surface reading: the best thing about someone from Texas, or a Texan dish's garnish
setter's reading: what a Texan wears on top of the head, a cowboy hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' sounds like praise or a food garnish; here it is literally headwear, the wide-brimmed hat of the cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic wide-brimmed cowboy hat is associated with Texas, so it is the headgear crowning a Texan.

clue.text: Old fellow in drawn contest

parts.note: stale means old, no longer fresh
a mate is a fellow or companion

explanation.surface: An elderly man takes part in a game that ends level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests a sketch; it means tied. The answer is a chess term for a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a position where the player to move has no legal move ends the game as a draw.

clue.text: Individual crossing for choice

parts.note: surface reading: a pedestrian picking which road crossing to use
setter's reading: someone marking an X on a ballot paper to pick a candidate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' suggests going across a road; it means putting a cross on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in an election makes a choice by marking a cross beside a name on the ballot.

clue.text: New Testament annunciation

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the following word is remade in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The angel's message to Mary as told in the Gospels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' reads as a single name tied to the Annunciation; 'New' asks for a fresh arrangement of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: An annunciation is a formal announcement or declaration, which is what a public declaration is.

clue.text: Delightful as a holiday resort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Praise for a pleasant seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: the adjective rhymes with 'dice', the place rhymes with 'piece'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pleasant, and the place is a well-known Mediterranean resort city on the Côte d'Azur.

clue.text: Superior, cold girl in charge

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lass is a girl
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A haughty, frosty young woman is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic is of the highest quality or standard, so it is first-rate and outstanding.

clue.text: He'll strive to study before exam — a hard worker

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a test is an exam
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A diligent student revises before an exam to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just puts the first piece ahead of the next. 'He'll strive' is a description standing for the person who competes.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a contest is someone who strives to win, so the person who will strive.

clue.text: Some men lean on a woman

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the run of words that follows, a portion tucked inside them

parts.note: the letters sit inside these words, running across the gaps

explanation.surface: Men rely on a woman for support.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'lean' through 'on' and 'a'. It is a woman's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anona is a female given name, so it stands for a woman, as names often do in crosswords.

clue.text: Foreign holy man to be seen on the mountains

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: An exotic guru is spotted up in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange in its older sense means alien or from elsewhere, as in a strange land or strangers.

clue.text: Plain net

definitions.meaning: first meaning: obvious, easy to see
second meaning: to make as profit after deductions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain net' looks like undecorated netting; both words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means evident and unambiguous, and also to earn as pure profit after costs, as in clearing a thousand pounds.

clue.text: Taking care perhaps with a palm

indicators.note: 'perhaps' implies the word shown is just one possible version, so its letters may be ordered otherwise

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone handling a palm tree with great attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged word is followed by the single letter from 'a'; 'perhaps' says the word shown is only one possible ordering of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a genus of tropical tree, the betel-nut tree among them, belonging to the palm family.

clue.text: Meeting a number on the track

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
on course means on the right track

explanation.surface: A gathering held where a runner with a number is on the racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a coming together of people or things, a gathering or assembly.

clue.text: 26 course
The keeper getting payment in advance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a servant or attendant, or a device that holds something
second meaning: a fee paid beforehand to secure services

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper or goalkeeper is paid up front.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old family servant and the fee paid ahead to engage a lawyer or adviser.

clue.text: Break apart, one is working

indicators.note: working suggests material being worked over and reshaped, so the letters are kneaded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something broke in two, but one piece still functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break apart' looks like one phrase; the definition is only 'Break', and 'working' means the letters are worked into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A separation is a parting or split, such as a couple's break or a break between two things.

clue.text: In time engineers concur

indicators.note: 'in' places the second item inside the first, read as 'with engineers in time'

parts.note: an age is a period of time
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Eventually the engineers come round to the same view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In time' reads as 'eventually', but 'In' places the engineers inside the word for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, which is a direct synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Gregarious type, though very green

parts.note: extra can mean very, as in extra large
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A sociable person who is nevertheless very inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very green' suggests a novice; heraldry's word for green is the second piece. This is an older spelling of extrovert.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing person who enjoys company is the psychological opposite of an introvert, so a sociable character.

clue.text: A reversible cushion on furniture makes it versatile

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something reversible can be turned round, so the word for the cushion is turned back to front

parts.note: a pad is a cushion
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A cushion that can be flipped and placed on a sofa is handy in many ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' sounds like a selling point of the cushion; it tells you to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something versatile can adjust easily to different uses or conditions.

clue.text: Electrify trains, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to thrill or carry away with emotion
second meaning: vehicles for carrying people, trains being one example

explanation.surface: A plan to convert the railway to electric power.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests railway electrification; 'Electrify' means to thrill, a sense of the verb, and trains are an example of the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to overwhelm with delight, and as a noun it covers vehicles such as trains.

clue.text: Watches discipline when personal complaint is made

parts.note: to eye is to watch
to train is to discipline

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on staff behaviour after a private grievance is lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, sore eyes from overuse are a physical ailment suffered by an individual, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Sums are set by a scholar

indicators.note: 'set' means arranged or put in order, so the letters are set out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic sets arithmetic problems for pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set by' reads like homework issued by a teacher; 'set' means the letters are set in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar and theologian.

clue.text: The main channel for blood supplies

definitions.text: The main channel for blood supplies

parts.words: The main channel for blood supplies
parts.note: surface reading: a principal route for delivering stocks to a blood bank
setter's reading: the body's largest artery, carrying blood from the heart

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like logistics for blood donations; it is anatomy, the principal vessel leaving the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: This great artery leaves the left ventricle and feeds oxygenated blood to the whole body through its branches.

clue.text: Push a boy into destructive behaviour

parts.note: to ram is to push forcefully
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: Shoving a youngster towards vandalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like an instruction to put one piece inside the other, but it only joins wordplay to definition. A page is a boy attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, wild behaviour that wrecks things, so destructive conduct.

clue.text: A fish — a fish found in seaweed

definitions.note: a description: the jelly is a substance extracted from seaweed

parts.note: taken as written
the gar is a long-snouted fish
taken as written
the gar again

explanation.surface: Two fish turn up tangled in a mass of seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition of 'a fish' gives the doubled form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This gelatinous substance is extracted from red algae and used in cooking and as a culture medium in laboratories.

clue.text: Grant for a minor

parts.note: taken as written
a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: Funding given to a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To award is to give or bestow formally, and as a noun it is a sum granted, so a close synonym.

clue.text: Article one's written on the French passage

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
I is one, with the S of the possessive
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a corridor in France.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church, theatre or aircraft.

clue.text: The way a dispenser creates an impression

definitions.text: The way a dispenser creates an impression

parts.words: The way a dispenser creates an impression
parts.note: surface reading: how a pharmacist or a server makes their mark on people
setter's reading: a post office machine issues postage labels, and the same word is the verb for pressing a mark

explanation.walkthrough: The word works two ways: what a post-office machine dispenses, and what you do to leave an imprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage labels come from a vending machine, and to press a design into a surface is the identically spelled verb.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment set up for a photograph

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'set up' means raised, so the word is written upwards from bottom to top

parts.note: pans are kitchen cookware

explanation.surface: Arranging cookware nicely for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means the word is written from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal word for a quickly taken snapshot or casual picture.

clue.text: Nowadays undertaking introduction

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a mission is a task undertaken

explanation.surface: These days, a project is being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let in, or the act of bringing someone into a place or group, is an introduction in the sense of entry.

clue.text: Make do with a single vegetable, nothing more

parts.note: one bean is a single vegetable
O looks like zero, nothing, added on

explanation.surface: Getting by on one vegetable and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make do' reads as 'manage'; the definition is just 'do', a party. A beano is a British slang word for a lively celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is an informal party, and a beano is a noisy jolly celebration in British slang.

clue.text: See how cinders may be utilised

indicators.note: things that may be utilised are put to a new purpose, so the letters are used to make a different word

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at the ways leftover ash from the fire can be put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be utilised' suggests the letters are put to a new use, made into another word.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or make out with the eyes or mind, so a close synonym for seeing.

clue.text: Show it's a real give-away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put on display or introduce
second meaning: a gift, something genuinely given away

explanation.surface: A performance that reveals everything about someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give-away' usually means a telltale sign; here it is literally something given.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to display or offer for view, and as a noun it means a gift.
